claims.claim: CD8+ T cells were reduced to a lesser extent in one-allele Stat5a-deficient mice compared to one-allele Stat5b-deficient mice.
claims.source: Frequencies of CD4+ T cells were comparable across all genotypes, whereas CD8+ T cells were reduced in one-allele Stat5b-deficient mice and, to a lesser extent, in one-allele Stat5a-deficient mice (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: B cells were increased in one-allele Stat5b-deficient mice.
claims.source: By contrast, B cells were increased in one-allele Stat5b-deficient mice and, consistent with the appearance of auto-antibodies, GL7+ Fashigh IgDlow germinal center (GC) B cells were dramatically enriched (Figure 2B–C and data not shown).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2B-C.

claims.claim: GL7+ Fashigh IgDlow germinal center (GC) B cells were dramatically enriched in one-allele Stat5b-deficient mice.
claims.source: By contrast, B cells were increased in one-allele Stat5b-deficient mice and, consistent with the appearance of auto-antibodies, GL7+ Fashigh IgDlow germinal center (GC) B cells were dramatically enriched (Figure 2B–C and data not shown).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2B-C.

claims.claim: One-allele Stat5a-deficient mice had a more modest accumulation of GC B cells compared to one-allele Stat5b-deficient mice.
claims.source: One-allele Stat5a-deficient mice had a more modest accumulation of GC B cells, again, illustrating both the relevance and redundancy of STAT5A (Figure 2B–C).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2B-C.

claims.claim: There was a marked accumulation of CD44high IL-7Rαlow effector/memory T cells in Stat5b-deficient mice.
claims.source: Not surprisingly, there was a marked accumulation of CD44high IL-7Rαlow effector/memory T cells in Stat5b-deficient mice which, as with the incidence of kidney disease, was more pronounced in those bearing one-allele of Stat5a than in those bearing two (Figure 3A-B & Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3A-B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: The accumulation of effector/memory T cells was more pronounced in Stat5b-deficient mice bearing one-allele of Stat5a than in those bearing two.
claims.source: Not surprisingly, there was a marked accumulation of CD44high IL-7Rαlow effector/memory T cells in Stat5b-deficient mice which, as with the incidence of kidney disease, was more pronounced in those bearing one-allele of Stat5a than in those bearing two (Figure 3A-B & Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3A-B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: IFN-ɣ+ cells were highly enriched in the autoimmune-prone Stat5b-deficient mice but not age-matched Stat5a-deficient counterparts.
claims.source: IFN-ɣ+ cells were highly enriched in the autoimmune-prone Stat5b-deficient mice but not age-matched Stat5a-deficient counterparts, suggesting that STAT5B may be particularly important for limiting Th1-type responses.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3C-D.

claims.claim: STAT5B may be particularly important for limiting Th1-type responses.
claims.source: IFN-ɣ+ cells were highly enriched in the autoimmune-prone Stat5b-deficient mice but not age-matched Stat5a-deficient counterparts, suggesting that STAT5B may be particularly important for limiting Th1-type responses.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the enrichment of IFN-ɣ+ cells in Stat5b-deficient mice.

claims.claim: IL-17A+ Th17-type cells were increased in Stat5b-deficient mice but this trend did not reach statistical significance.
claims.source: IL-17A+ Th17-type cells were also increased but this trend did not reach statistical significance (Figure 3C–D).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3C-D.

claims.claim: There was dramatic accumulation of PD1high CXCR5high ICOShigh Tfh cells in one-allele Stat5b-deficient mice.
claims.source: Mirroring the abundance of GC B cells, there was dramatic accumulation of PD1high CXCR5high ICOShigh Tfh cells in one-allele Stat5b-deficient mice, and a more modest enrichment in one-allele Stat5a-deficient mice (Figure 3E–F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B & data not shown).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3E-F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: There was a more modest enrichment of Tfh cells in one-allele Stat5a-deficient mice compared to one-allele Stat5b-deficient mice.
claims.source: Mirroring the abundance of GC B cells, there was dramatic accumulation of PD1high CXCR5high ICOShigh Tfh cells in one-allele Stat5b-deficient mice, and a more modest enrichment in one-allele Stat5a-deficient mice (Figure 3E–F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B & data not shown).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3E-F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Mice lacking one-allele each of Stat5a and Stat5b (double-heterozygotes) had more Tfh cells than those lacking two-alleles of Stat5a.
claims.source: Consistent with the latter view, mice lacking one-allele each of Stat5a and Stat5b (i.e. double-heterozygotes) had more Tfh cells than those lacking two-alleles of Stat5a, despite having the same total number of alleles.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: The percentage of Tfh cells was comparable between two-allele Stat5b-deficient mice and one-allele Stat5a-deficient mice.
claims.source: Moreover, the percentage of Tfh cells was comparable between two-allele Stat5b-deficient mice and one-allele Stat5a-deficient mice, suggesting that two alleles of Stat5a are roughly equal to one allele of Stat5b (Figure 3F & Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Two alleles of Stat5a are roughly equal to one allele of Stat5b in terms of Tfh cell regulation.
claims.source: Moreover, the percentage of Tfh cells was comparable between two-allele Stat5b-deficient mice and one-allele Stat5a-deficient mice, suggesting that two alleles of Stat5a are roughly equal to one allele of Stat5b (Figure 3F & Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the comparable Tfh cell percentages between the two genotypes.

claims.claim: STAT5 is essential for Treg cells.
claims.source: CD4+ T regulatory (Treg) cells expressing the forkhead transcription factor, FOXP3, are essential for immunological tolerance (Malek and Castro, 2010). Given the importance of STAT5 in Treg cells (Mahmud et al., 2013), we next inspected this subset.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Malek and Castro, 2010 and Mahmud et al., 2013.

claims.claim: STAT5-null mice exhibit a profound lack of Treg cells.
claims.source: Unlike STAT5-null mice, which exhibit a profound lack of Treg cells (Yao et al., 2007; Burchill et al., 2006), frequencies of splenic FOXP3+ cells were relatively normal across our STAT5 mutants.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Yao et al., 2007; Burchill et al., 2006.

claims.claim: Frequencies of splenic FOXP3+ cells were relatively normal across STAT5 mutants.
claims.source: Unlike STAT5-null mice, which exhibit a profound lack of Treg cells (Yao et al., 2007; Burchill et al., 2006), frequencies of splenic FOXP3+ cells were relatively normal across our STAT5 mutants.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Absolute counts of Treg cells were significantly lower in one-allele Stat5b-deficient mice.
claims.source: However, due to differences in overall cellularity, absolute counts were significantly lower in one- and two-allele Stat5b-deficient mice, as well one-allele Stat5a-deficient mice.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Absolute counts of Treg cells were significantly lower in two-allele Stat5b-deficient mice.
claims.source: However, due to differences in overall cellularity, absolute counts were significantly lower in one- and two-allele Stat5b-deficient mice, as well one-allele Stat5a-deficient mice.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Absolute counts of Treg cells were significantly lower in one-allele Stat5a-deficient mice.
claims.source: However, due to differences in overall cellularity, absolute counts were significantly lower in one- and two-allele Stat5b-deficient mice, as well one-allele Stat5a-deficient mice.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: IL-2Rα is a component of the IL-2 receptor that is critical for Treg cell homeostasis and function.
claims.source: To further characterize the Treg compartment, we measured IL-2Rα, a component of the IL-2 receptor that is critical for Treg cell homeostasis and function. It is also a both upstream and downstream of STAT5 signaling and, thus, can be viewed as an indicator of STAT5 activity (Malek and Castro, 2010).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Malek and Castro, 2010.

claims.claim: IL-2Rα is both upstream and downstream of STAT5 signaling.
claims.source: To further characterize the Treg compartment, we measured IL-2Rα, a component of the IL-2 receptor that is critical for Treg cell homeostasis and function. It is also a both upstream and downstream of STAT5 signaling and, thus, can be viewed as an indicator of STAT5 activity (Malek and Castro, 2010).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Malek and Castro, 2010.

claims.claim: IL-2Rα can be viewed as an indicator of STAT5 activity.
claims.source: To further characterize the Treg compartment, we measured IL-2Rα, a component of the IL-2 receptor that is critical for Treg cell homeostasis and function. It is also a both upstream and downstream of STAT5 signaling and, thus, can be viewed as an indicator of STAT5 activity (Malek and Castro, 2010).
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the relationship between IL-2Rα and STAT5 signaling, supported by citation to Malek and Castro, 2010.

claims.claim: The percentage of IL-2Rα+ Treg cells mirrored the total number of Stat5 alleles.
claims.source: We found that the percentage of IL-2Rα+ Treg cells mirrored the total number of Stat5 alleles; it was slightly reduced in mice with three alleles, lower in those with 2, and lower still in those with 1 (Figure 4A–B).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4A-B.

claims.claim: Residual IL-2Rα+ Treg cells from one-allele mice had reduced suppressive capacity.
claims.source: We also noted that residual IL-2Rα+ Treg cells from one-allele mice had reduced suppressive capacity and were unable to maintain expression of IL-2Rα during in vitro culture (Figure 4C–E).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4C-E.

claims.claim: Residual IL-2Rα+ Treg cells from one-allele mice were unable to maintain expression of IL-2Rα during in vitro culture.
claims.source: We also noted that residual IL-2Rα+ Treg cells from one-allele mice had reduced suppressive capacity and were unable to maintain expression of IL-2Rα during in vitro culture (Figure 4C–E).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4C-E.

claims.claim: The reduced suppressive capacity and IL-2Rα maintenance phenotypes were more pronounced in the absence of Stat5b than Stat5a.
claims.source: Each of these phenotypes was more pronounced in the absence of Stat5b than Stat5a, again, illustrating both the dominance of the former and the relevance (and/or redundancy) of the latter.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4C-E.

claims.claim: TBX21 is a transcription factor required for Treg cells to limit Th1-type responses.
claims.source: Given the appearance of IFN-ɣ+ effector T cells in Stat5b-deficient mice, we next asked whether Stat5b-deficient Treg cells express TBX21, a transcription factor required for Treg cells to limit Th1-type responses (Koch et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Koch et al., 2009.

claims.claim: IL-2 was sufficient to induce TBX21 in WT Treg cells.
claims.source: Similar to conventional T cells (Liao et al., 2011), we found that IL-2 was sufficient to induce TBX21 in WT Treg cells (Figure 4F).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4F and supported by citation to Liao et al., 2011.

claims.claim: IL-2-induced TBX21 expression was slightly reduced in the absence of Stat5a.
claims.source: This effect was slightly reduced in the absence of Stat5a but almost completely abolished in the absence of Stat5b, consistent with the disparity of other STAT5-dependent parameters (e.g. T cell and Th1 cell frequencies).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4F-G.

claims.claim: IL-2-induced TBX21 expression was almost completely abolished in the absence of Stat5b.
claims.source: This effect was slightly reduced in the absence of Stat5a but almost completely abolished in the absence of Stat5b, consistent with the disparity of other STAT5-dependent parameters (e.g. T cell and Th1 cell frequencies).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4F-G.

claims.claim: Both Stat5a- and Stat5b-deficient Treg cells maintained FOXP3 expression similar to WT controls.
claims.source: Both Stat5a- and Stat5b-deficient Treg cells maintained FOXP3 expression similar to WT controls and, surprisingly, both gained the ability to produce IL-2, a cytokine that is typically restricted in this lineage (Figure 4F–G).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4F-G.

claims.claim: Both Stat5a- and Stat5b-deficient Treg cells gained the ability to produce IL-2.
claims.source: Both Stat5a- and Stat5b-deficient Treg cells maintained FOXP3 expression similar to WT controls and, surprisingly, both gained the ability to produce IL-2, a cytokine that is typically restricted in this lineage (Figure 4F–G).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4F-G.

claims.claim: IL-2 is typically restricted in Treg cells.
claims.source: Both Stat5a- and Stat5b-deficient Treg cells maintained FOXP3 expression similar to WT controls and, surprisingly, both gained the ability to produce IL-2, a cytokine that is typically restricted in this lineage (Figure 4F–G).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about Treg cell biology.

claims.claim: STAT5 is required for in vitro differentiation of induced regulatory (iTreg) T cells.
claims.source: STAT5 is required for in vitro differentiation of induced regulatory (iTreg) T cells (Yao et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Yao et al., 2007.

claims.claim: There were far fewer FOXP3+ cells in one-allele Stat5b-deficient iTreg cultures than in one-allele Stat5a-deficient cultures.
claims.source: We found that, although both paralogs appear to play a role, there were far fewer FOXP3+ cells in one-allele Stat5b-deficient cultures than in (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: Deletion of either Stat5a or Stat5b endowed FOXP3+ iTreg cells with the ability to produce IL-2.
claims.source: We also found that deletion of either paralog endowed FOXP3+ iTreg cells with the ability to produce IL-2, which suggests that, beyond differentiation, STAT5 may limit the inflammatory potential of this subset (Figure 5A–B).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5A-B.

claims.claim: STAT5 may limit the inflammatory potential of iTreg cells.
claims.source: We also found that deletion of either paralog endowed FOXP3+ iTreg cells with the ability to produce IL-2, which suggests that, beyond differentiation, STAT5 may limit the inflammatory potential of this subset (Figure 5A–B).
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that STAT5-deficient iTreg cells produce IL-2.

claims.claim: The overall Treg gene signature was similarly affected in both Stat5a- and Stat5b-deficient T cells cultured under iTreg polarizing conditions.
claims.source: Gene set enrichment analysis revealed that the overall Treg gene signature - defined by a combination of FOXP3- and IL-2-dependent transcriptional programs (Hill et al., 2007) - was similarly affected in both genotypes, meaning that there were no broad qualitative differences (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on GSEA analysis shown in Figure 5C and supported by citation to Hill et al., 2007.

claims.claim: There were obvious quantitative differences in Treg gene expression between Stat5a- and Stat5b-deficient T cells.
claims.source: However, there were obvious quantitative differences; several key genes, including Foxp3 and Il2ra, were more affected by the loss of STAT5B than STAT5A (Figure 5D).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claims.claim: Foxp3 and Il2ra were more affected by the loss of STAT5B than STAT5A in iTreg cells.
claims.source: However, there were obvious quantitative differences; several key genes, including Foxp3 and Il2ra, were more affected by the loss of STAT5B than STAT5A (Figure 5D).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claims.claim: Deletion of Stat5b is more disruptive to Treg cell biology than deletion of Stat5a.
claims.source: Thus, while both paralogs can impact Treg cell biology, deletion of Stat5b is clearly more disruptive, befitting its dominant station within immunological tolerance.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the cumulative data on Treg cell phenotypes in Stat5a- and Stat5b-deficient mice.

claims.claim: Stat5a- and Stat5b-deficient cells typically clustered together and equidistant from WT controls in multidimensional scaling analysis.
claims.source: We began our transcriptomic survey by performing multidimensional scaling of the datasets, thereby gaining a broad overview of the experimental groups. Stat5a- and Stat5b-deficient cells typically clustered together and equidistant from WT controls, suggesting that the loss of either paralog has comparable genome-wide effects (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on MDS analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: The loss of either Stat5a or Stat5b has comparable genome-wide effects on gene expression.
claims.source: We began our transcriptomic survey by performing multidimensional scaling of the datasets, thereby gaining a broad overview of the experimental groups. Stat5a- and Stat5b-deficient cells typically clustered together and equidistant from WT controls, suggesting that the loss of either paralog has comparable genome-wide effects (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the MDS analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Most genes designated as STAT5B-specific were also affected by the loss of STAT5A, albeit to a lesser degree.
claims.source: However, upon close inspection, we concluded that this disparity was largely due to the arbitrary fold-change cutoff that was used. Most genes that were designated as STAT5B-specific were also affected by the loss of STAT5A (and vice versa), albeit to a lesser degree that did not reach our 2-fold threshold (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: The majority of STAT5-sensitive genes were affected by both STAT5A and STAT5B.
claims.source: This analysis revealed a binomial distribution for all experimental conditions. The majority of genes were in central bins, affected by both STAT5A and STAT5B, while membership in peripheral bins decreased steadily as paralog preference increased.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on paralog preference analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: All paralog preference curves were shifted towards STAT5B.
claims.source: Importantly, all curves were shifted towards STAT5B, suggesting that STAT5-sensitive genes are generally more impacted by STAT5B than STAT5A (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on paralog preference analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: STAT5-sensitive genes are generally more impacted by STAT5B than STAT5A.
claims.source: Importantly, all curves were shifted towards STAT5B, suggesting that STAT5-sensitive genes are generally more impacted by STAT5B than STAT5A (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the paralog preference analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: IL-2-driven induction of IL-2Rα was clearly more diminished in Stat5b-deficient cells than in Stat5a-deficient counterparts.
claims.source: This latter trend was also evident at the protein level; IL-2-driven (but not IL-6-driven) induction of IL-2Rα was clearly more diminished in Stat5b-deficient cells than in Stat5a-deficient counterparts (Figure 6E).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6E.

claims.claim: IL-6-driven induction of IL-2Rα was not differentially affected in Stat5a- versus Stat5b-deficient cells.
claims.source: This latter trend was also evident at the protein level; IL-2-driven (but not IL-6-driven) induction of IL-2Rα was clearly more diminished in Stat5b-deficient cells than in Stat5a-deficient counterparts (Figure 6E).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6E.

claims.claim: STAT5B is dominant over STAT5A in helper T cells.
claims.source: Collectively, these data affirm that STAT5B is dominant over STAT5A while, at the same time, demonstrating pervasive redundancy at the level of gene transcription.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the cumulative transcriptomic data.

claims.claim: There is pervasive redundancy between STAT5A and STAT5B at the level of gene transcription.
claims.source: Collectively, these data affirm that STAT5B is dominant over STAT5A while, at the same time, demonstrating pervasive redundancy at the level of gene transcription.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the cumulative transcriptomic data.

claims.claim: Between 12% and 22% of all STAT5-sensitive genes can be classified as paralog-specific.
claims.source: Using strict analysis criteria, we discovered that between 12% and 22% of all STAT5-sensitive genes can be classified as paralog-specific, meaning that they are solely dependent on either STAT5A or STAT5B.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: The absolute number of paralog-specific genes varied across cell states and stimuli.
claims.source: The absolute number of paralog-specific genes varied across cell states and stimuli, with the largest allotment found in IL-7-treated naive cells, and was typically skewed towards STAT5B (Figure 6C & Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on analysis shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1E.

results.result: A single allele of either Stat5a or Stat5b is sufficient to prevent perinatal lethality in mice. All 8 genotypes of STAT5 mutant mice were born at expected Mendelian ratios and survived beyond 6 months of age.
results.evaluation: Claims C26-C28 demonstrate that mice with various combinations of Stat5 alleles (ranging from 1 to 4 total alleles) survive to adulthood, unlike STAT5-null mice which exhibit perinatal lethality. The data are supported by citations and consistent with prior work, though the primary data are noted as 'not shown'.

results.result: A single allele of either Stat5a or Stat5b supports erythropoiesis, but white blood cell counts are differentially affected by paralog deficiency. WBC counts were sharply reduced in one-allele Stat5a- or Stat5b-deficient mice and two-allele Stat5b-deficient mice, but relatively normal in two-allele Stat5a-deficient mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C29-C34 are supported by experimental data in Figure 1B showing comparable RBC counts and hematocrits across genotypes, but differential WBC counts. The data clearly demonstrate that Stat5b has greater impact on WBC counts than Stat5a, supporting the dominance hypothesis.

results.result: Stat5b-deficient mice develop autoimmune kidney disease with penetrance dependent on Stat5a allele dosage. Afflicted mice present with loss of glomerular structure, proteinuria, and anti-DNA antibodies, demonstrating that Stat5b is required for immunological tolerance with evidence of redundancy/cooperativity with Stat5a.
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C41 are supported by histological and biochemical data in Figure 1C-F. The dose-dependent penetrance (75% with one Stat5a allele vs 25% with two) provides strong evidence for both Stat5b dominance and Stat5a redundancy/cooperativity. The autoimmune phenotype is well-characterized.

results.result: Lymphoid organ cellularity is reduced in STAT5-deficient mice in a dose-dependent manner. Stat5b-deficient mice show greater reduction in splenocyte counts than Stat5a-deficient mice, though Stat5a also has substantial influence. All genotypes with fewer than three STAT5 alleles show reduced lymph node cellularity.
results.evaluation: Claims C42-C46 are supported by experimental data in Figure 2A showing dose-dependent effects on lymphoid cellularity. The data demonstrate both Stat5b dominance and Stat5a contribution, consistent with the overall model. Statistical significance is indicated in the figures.

results.result: STAT5 deficiency differentially affects lymphocyte subset frequencies. CD4+ T cell frequencies remain comparable across genotypes, while CD8+ T cells are reduced in Stat5b-deficient mice. B cells and germinal center B cells are dramatically enriched in Stat5b-deficient mice, with more modest accumulation in Stat5a-deficient mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C47-C52 are supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2B-C. The differential effects on lymphocyte subsets are clearly demonstrated and consistent with the autoimmune phenotype. The data show both qualitative and quantitative differences between Stat5a and Stat5b deficiency.

results.result: Stat5b-deficient mice accumulate effector/memory T cells and IFN-γ+ Th1 cells in a Stat5a dose-dependent manner. The accumulation is more pronounced in mice with one Stat5a allele versus two, and IFN-γ+ cells are enriched specifically in Stat5b-deficient mice, suggesting Stat5b is particularly important for limiting Th1 responses.
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C57 are supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3A-D. The dose-dependent effects and paralog-specific enrichment of IFN-γ+ cells provide strong evidence for Stat5b dominance in controlling effector T cell responses. However, C56 is somewhat speculative as it uses 'may be' language.

results.result: T follicular helper (Tfh) cells accumulate dramatically in Stat5b-deficient mice with dose-dependent effects of Stat5a. Comparison across genotypes suggests that two alleles of Stat5a are roughly equivalent to one allele of Stat5b in terms of Tfh cell regulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C58-C62 are supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3E-F showing dramatic Tfh accumulation. The quantitative comparison between genotypes (C60-C62) provides strong evidence for the dose-dependent model, though the equivalence calculation (C62) involves some inference from the data.

results.result: STAT5 mutant mice maintain relatively normal frequencies of FOXP3+ Treg cells, unlike STAT5-null mice which lack Treg cells. However, absolute Treg cell counts are significantly reduced in one- and two-allele Stat5b-deficient mice and one-allele Stat5a-deficient mice due to overall reduced cellularity.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C68 are supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and citations to prior work. The distinction between frequency and absolute counts is important and well-documented. The data show that partial STAT5 deficiency has different effects than complete deficiency.

results.result: IL-2Rα expression on Treg cells mirrors total STAT5 allele number, and residual IL-2Rα+ Treg cells from one-allele mice have reduced suppressive capacity and cannot maintain IL-2Rα expression in culture. These phenotypes are more pronounced in Stat5b-deficient than Stat5a-deficient mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C75 are supported by experimental data in Figure 4A-E including suppression assays and in vitro culture experiments. The dose-dependent effects on IL-2Rα expression and functional capacity provide strong evidence for STAT5 as a limiting factor in Treg function.

results.result: IL-2 induces TBX21 expression in WT Treg cells, an effect that is slightly reduced in Stat5a-deficient but almost abolished in Stat5b-deficient Treg cells. Both Stat5a- and Stat5b-deficient Treg cells maintain FOXP3 but gain the ability to produce IL-2, a cytokine typically restricted in this lineage.
results.evaluation: Claims C76-C82 are supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4F-G and citations to prior work. The differential effects on TBX21 induction and the unexpected IL-2 production provide mechanistic insights into Treg dysfunction. The data are consistent with the overall paralog dominance model.

results.result: In vitro iTreg differentiation is impaired in STAT5-deficient cells, with far fewer FOXP3+ cells in Stat5b-deficient cultures than Stat5a-deficient cultures. Deletion of either paralog endows iTreg cells with the ability to produce IL-2, suggesting STAT5 may limit inflammatory potential.
results.evaluation: Claims C83-C86 are supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5A-B. The differential effects on iTreg differentiation and the IL-2 production phenotype are clearly demonstrated. However, C86 is somewhat speculative ('may limit') and would benefit from additional functional validation.

results.result: The overall Treg gene signature is similarly affected in Stat5a- and Stat5b-deficient iTreg cultures, but there are quantitative differences with key genes like Foxp3 and Il2ra more affected by loss of STAT5B. Deletion of Stat5b is more disruptive to Treg biology than deletion of Stat5a.
results.evaluation: Claims C87-C90 are supported by GSEA and RNA-seq data in Figure 5C-D. The distinction between qualitative similarity and quantitative differences is important and well-supported. The conclusion about Stat5b being more disruptive (C90) is a reasonable inference from the cumulative data.

results.result: Multidimensional scaling analysis shows Stat5a- and Stat5b-deficient cells cluster together equidistant from WT controls, suggesting comparable genome-wide effects. However, most genes designated as paralog-specific are affected by both paralogs to different degrees, and paralog preference curves are shifted toward STAT5B.
results.evaluation: Claims C91-C96 are supported by MDS and paralog preference analyses in Figure 6 and supplementary figures. The data demonstrate that apparent paralog specificity is largely due to arbitrary fold-change cutoffs, and that STAT5B generally has greater quantitative impact. This is a key finding supporting the dose model.

results.result: IL-2-driven induction of IL-2Rα protein is more diminished in Stat5b-deficient cells than Stat5a-deficient cells, while IL-6-driven induction is not differentially affected. Collectively, the data affirm STAT5B dominance while demonstrating pervasive redundancy at the transcriptional level.
results.evaluation: Claims C97-C100 are supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 6E and the cumulative transcriptomic analyses. The IL-6 control (C98) is important for demonstrating specificity. The conclusions about dominance and redundancy (C99-C100) are well-supported by the comprehensive dataset.

results.result: Between 12-22% of STAT5-sensitive genes are paralog-specific, with the largest number in IL-7-treated naive cells and typically skewed toward STAT5B. The authors propose that phenotypic differences are due largely to paralog preference (quantitative differences) rather than paralog-specific effects (qualitative differences).
results.evaluation: Claims C101-C105 are supported by analyses in Figure 6C and supplementary figures. The identification of paralog-specific genes using strict criteria is methodologically sound. However, C105 is a proposed model that, while well-supported by the data, represents an interpretation rather than a direct observation.

results.result: ChIP-seq analysis reveals 1275 STAT5 binding sites in WT cells, with progressively fewer peaks in Stat5a/bhet (658), Stat5a-deficient (609), and Stat5b-deficient (97) cells. The reduced peak numbers and intensities indicate that STAT5 availability impacts genomic distribution even when both paralogs are present.
results.evaluation: Claims C106-C111 are supported by ChIP-seq data in Figure 7A and 7D. The dramatic reduction in peaks in Stat5b-deficient cells compared to Stat5a-deficient cells provides strong evidence for Stat5b dominance at the chromatin level. The inference about STAT5 availability (C109) is well-supported.

results.result: STAT5 peaks are similarly localized across genotypes, typically near transcriptional start sites but also at distal regions >100 kb away, and are highly enriched for STAT-binding motifs. Most peaks in Stat5b-deficient cells match peaks in other genotypes.
results.evaluation: Claims C112-C116 are supported by ChIP-seq analyses in Figure 7B-C and supplementary figures. The consistent localization patterns and motif enrichment across genotypes support the redundancy model. The peak overlap analysis (C116) demonstrates that Stat5b-independent binding occurs at a subset of sites.

results.result: STAT5B-independent peaks occur near genes that are highly occupied in WT controls and highly dysregulated in Stat5b-deficient cells, suggesting only the most robust (high-affinity) STAT5-binding sites are preserved in the absence of Stat5b.
results.evaluation: Claims C117-C118 are supported by integrated ChIP-seq and RNA-seq analysis in Figure 8. The correlation between peak intensity in WT cells and preservation in Stat5b-deficient cells provides strong evidence for an affinity-based hierarchy. This is a key mechanistic insight.

results.result: STAT5 binds to and regulates key target genes including Il2ra (critical for Treg function) and Bcl6 (master regulator of Tfh differentiation). STAT5 binding to Bcl6 appears to be a negative regulatory event, as STAT5 can suppress Bcl6 expression in T cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C119-C124 are supported by ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data in Figure 7E and supplementary figures, along with citations to prior work. The identification of these specific targets provides mechanistic links to the observed phenotypes. The negative regulation of Bcl6 (C123-C124) is well-supported by multiple studies.

results.result: Stat5b is more abundant than Stat5a at both mRNA and protein levels in T cells. Removing one Stat5b allele has greater impact on total STAT5 protein than removing one Stat5a allele, and similar trends are observed for phosphorylated STAT5. STAT5B makes a greater contribution to the total STAT5 protein pool.
results.evaluation: Claims C125-C129 are supported by transcriptome analysis (Figure 9—figure supplement 1) and flow cytometry data (Figure 9A-B). The consistent findings across multiple datasets and protein measurements provide strong evidence for differential expression as the basis for functional dominance. This is a central finding of the paper.

results.result: Ectopic STAT5A expression in Stat5b-deficient T cells mobilizes 320 genes, mostly pan-STAT5 genes that do not show paralog preference and are enriched for both STAT5A- and STAT5B-dependent gene sets. This supports the idea that STAT5 protein concentration differences underlie transcriptomic divergence between Stat5a- and Stat5b-deficient cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C130-C134 are supported by RNA-seq and GSEA analyses in Figure 10A-C. The rescue experiment is well-designed and provides strong evidence for the quantitative model. The lack of paralog preference in rescued genes (C132) is particularly important for demonstrating functional equivalence at sufficient concentrations.

results.result: FOXP3 expression is reduced in Stat5a/bhet and almost abolished in Stat5b-deficient iTreg cultures, but ectopic STAT5A restores FOXP3 to comparable levels across genotypes. There is a clear linear correlation between STAT5 and FOXP3 protein levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C135-C138 are supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 10D. The rescue of FOXP3 expression by ectopic STAT5A and the linear correlation between STAT5 and FOXP3 provide strong evidence for a dose-dependent threshold model. This is a key functional validation of the quantitative hypothesis.

results.result: IL-2Rα expression is diminished in Stat5a/bhet and Stat5b-deficient iTreg cultures but restored by ectopic STAT5A. The data argue that a threshold STAT5 concentration must be reached to institute the Treg program, and that STAT5 is a limiting resource for this process.
results.evaluation: Claims C139-C142 are supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 10E and the effect of ectopic STAT5A on WT cells. The threshold model (C141-C142) is a reasonable inference from the dose-response data, though it involves some interpretation beyond direct observation.

results.result: IL-17+ cells are dramatically increased in Stat5-deficient Th17 cultures (4-fold in Stat5a/bhet, >25-fold in Stat5b-deficient), and ectopic STAT5A both extinguishes IL-17 and induces FOXP3, demonstrating that STAT5 concentration can tip the balance between effector and regulatory T cell programs.
results.evaluation: Claims C143-C147 are supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 10—figure supplement 1B. The dramatic effects on Th17/Treg balance provide strong functional evidence for the dose-dependent model. The ability of ectopic STAT5A to reverse the phenotype is particularly compelling.

results.result: STAT5B is dominant for both effector and regulatory T cell responses and is uniquely necessary for immunological tolerance. This conclusion is based on the cumulative experimental data showing greater impact of Stat5b deficiency on multiple T cell functions and the autoimmune phenotype.
results.evaluation: Claims C148-C149 represent the major conclusions of the study, inferred from the comprehensive dataset including phenotypic, transcriptomic, and chromatin analyses. The conclusions are well-supported by the cumulative evidence, though they represent high-level interpretations of the data.

results.result: The authors propose a quantitative model where asymmetric expression (paralog dose) rather than distinct functional properties is the key distinguishing feature between STAT5A and STAT5B. Relative abundance imposes functional specificity in the face of widespread structural homology.
results.evaluation: Claims C150-C151 represent the central model proposed by the authors, supported by the comprehensive genomic, transcriptomic, and functional data. While the model is well-supported, it represents an interpretation and synthesis of the data rather than a direct observation. The model successfully explains the observed phenotypes and is consistent with all major findings.
